aerospace-engineering-minor.summary: The CoursePlan file has the right overall shape: four core courses with MAE 3050 or MAE 4060 required, and two Group B/C courses. Its course lists are out of date against the 2026-2027 catalog. Group A is missing several catalog core courses: ENGRG 3400, MAE 4070, MAE 4161, MAE 4231, the MAE 4440/4441/5440 family and the MAE 4540/5540 family. Group B is missing MAE 4021, MAE 4131 and MAE 5770, and still accepts MAE 5130 and MAE 6510, which the catalog no longer lists. The B/C requirement demands exactly two B/C courses, but the catalog only caps them at two, so extra core courses should be able to fill those spots. The footnote rules for MAE 4900 (at least 3 credits, advisor form, at most one of MAE 4291/4900) are not mentioned. The ME-major rule requiring two aerospace courses from the ME Major Approved Electives list is absent. The other prose rules (18-credit minimum, no overlap with the ME minor or early M.Eng. courses, one outside course by petition) are not shown to students.

animal-science-minor.summary: The data file has one 15-credit requirement that accepts BIOAP 1100 and ANSC 1000–4999 courses, excluding ANSC 49**. It gets the 15-credit total and the Special Studies exclusion roughly right. It is missing the catalog's rule that at least one of the four core courses (BIOAP 1100, ANSC 2400, ANSC 2120, ANSC 2210) must be completed. It also does not mention the limit of 3 credits (1 course) shared with the student's major, or the ban on sharing courses with another minor. Its checker rejects 5000+ level ANSC courses even though the catalog sets no level limit.

anthropology-ba.summary: The Anthropology data file has the catalog's structure: three subfields, ANTHR 3000, two 3000-level courses, two 4000-level courses and two electives (ten courses). The subfield course lists are out of date, though. The Sociocultural slot accepts ANTHR 2421, which the catalog no longer lists. The Biological slot is missing ANTHR 3235 (Bioarchaeology), which the catalog now lists. The elective checker also accepts only ANTHR courses, while its own warning implies advisor-approved cognate courses can count. The source URL points to an older catalog edition.

applied-economics-management-bs.summary: The AEM data file is substantially out of date against the 2026-2027 catalog. Several things are missing: AEM 2700, AEM 3205 and AEM 1101 from the core, and the full calculus list. The quantitative-methods and applied-economics category lists are stale. The Grand Challenges sequence still uses the old three-part structure. The concentration set no longer matches the catalog: Agribusiness Management is retired, the EERE, Food and International concentrations are renamed and restructured, the Business Analytics electives match nothing, and the Strategy counts are swapped. The CALS-credit minimum is 55 instead of 75. Many course lists add retired courses and omit current ones.

applied-economics-minor.summary: The data file for the Applied Economics minor is out of date. The Applied Economics, Various Topics list is missing four catalog courses: AEM 4100, AEM 4110, AEM 4190 and AEM 4880. It also accepts AEM 4515, which the catalog no longer lists. The Economic Theory or Practice requirement accepts ECON 3030 and PUBPOL 2000 for every student, but the catalog limits them to Economics and Public Policy majors. Economics majors need four Various Topics courses, not three. The description also misstates the JCB credit rule. The introductory economics requirement matches.

applied-mathematics-minor.summary: CoursePlan correctly encodes the MATH 2930 and MATH 2940 requirement. It treats the six-course group requirement as a self-check, which is acceptable, and its description repeats the catalog's four group rules accurately. However, that description leaves out the catalog's note excluding MATH 4200 together with MAE 5790/MATH 4210. It also omits the group course lists and the Group 6 exceptions. Both source links point to old MAE pages (including a 2019 PDF) rather than the catalog. None of these differences changes what the checker counts.

artificial-intelligence-minor.summary: The data file is badly out of date against the 2026-2027 catalog. Every core slot accepts courses the catalog no longer lists and rejects most of the courses it does list. The Ethics slot accepts none of the catalog options. The elective list overlaps the catalog only partly: it omits about 35 approved electives and accepts core courses and unrelated courses. Both requirements set allowCourseDoubleCounting, so one course can fill a core slot and an elective slot, although the catalog requires six courses and its footnotes forbid that overlap. The catalog's 15-credit minimum and its rule allowing at most two courses to overlap with the major are not encoded anywhere.

astronomy-ba.summary: The CoursePlan file has the right overall structure: introductory physics, introductory math, an experimental course, and a toggleable Astrophysics or General Astronomy concentration. It differs from the 2026-2027 catalog in several places that change what counts. In the core, the PHYS 2218 option does not require PHYS 2210, and the math slot accepts MATH 1120 and MATH 1220, which the catalog does not list. In the Astrophysics concentration, ASTRO 4434 is missing and the required ASTRO 4410 is not enforced. The math slot also accepts any MATH course instead of the required AEP 3200 and AEP 4200. In the General Astronomy concentration, ASTRO 4523 is missing from the elective group, and the 15-credit External Complementary Area is not represented at all.

astronomy-minor.summary: The checkers match the catalog. Fifteen credits are required from ASTRO courses at the 3000 level or above plus ASTRO 2211, 2212, 2290 and 2299, and a second requirement checks for at least 6 credits at the 3000+ level, with double counting correctly allowed. The only difference is that the first requirement's description adds a letter-grade rule (6 of the 15 credits not S/U) that the catalog does not state.

atmospheric-science-bs.summary: The Core and Computer Science requirements match the catalog, but the rest of the file is out of date. Statistics accepts only AEM 2100, not the catalog's EAS 4350 or STSCI 2100. Chemistry requires CHEM 1560 instead of CHEM 2070 & CHEM 2071. Physics omits the PHYS 1112 and PHYS 2213 alternatives. Electives count 2 courses instead of 6 credits, accept EAS 1340, EAS 4570, EAS 4960 and EAS 4980, which the catalog does not list as electives, and reject EAS 5555. Mathematics accepts MATH 2130, which the catalog does not list.

biological-engineering-bs.summary: The be.ts file has several serious errors against the 2026-2027 catalog. The 'Biochemistry' requirement checks CHEM 2070/2080 or CHEM 2150 instead of the BIOMG biochemistry options. BIOSM 1610 and CHEME 3230 are missing as alternatives. CHEM 3530 is accepted for Organic Chemistry. The capstone (BEE 4590 or BEE 4530) has no slot of its own. The 15-credit Biological Sciences elective, Major-Approved Electives and ENGRG 1050 are absent. The focus-area requirements count 4 courses instead of credits and describe 7 outdated focus areas instead of the catalog's 5.

biology-society-ba.summary: The bsoc.ts file has the same overall structure as the 2026-2027 catalog: intro bio, calculus, statistics, ethics, the social sciences/humanities foundation, biology breadth and depth, core, and theme. However, many of its course lists are out of date. The Core requirement is missing BSOC 2071 and accepts four courses the catalog does not list. Statistics accepts MATH 1710, which the catalog does not list. General Chemistry is enforced as required although the catalog only recommends it for pre-health students. Every foundation and theme list is missing current catalog courses and accepts retired or non-listed courses. The senior seminar's open 4000-level option and the rule that lets senior seminars count as theme electives are not represented.

biomedical-engineering-bs.summary: The BME data file is out of date against the 2026-2027 catalog. In the core, the checker drops BME 2210 and BME 2080 and still requires BME 2310, which has not been offered since SP21. The statistics option rejects STSCI 2150 and accepts CEE 3040, which the catalog does not list. In the concentrations, every option requires 6 elective courses where the catalog requires 6 credits. MCSE checks BME 3020 instead of BME 3110. BMMB rejects the CHEM 1570 alternative to PHYS 2214. Every elective list is missing many catalog courses and some accept courses the catalog no longer lists. Several descriptions, the 13-credit figure and the 'Engineering Distriubtions' requirement also disagree with the catalog.

business-minor.summary: The Statistics requirement accepts the wrong courses. It rejects AEM 2100 and CRP 1200, which the catalog lists. It accepts AEM 1200 and MATH 1710, which the catalog does not; AEM 1200 is really the Introduction to Management course. Introduction to Marketing is missing NCC 4530. The Microeconomics, Management, Accounting and Finance course lists match once cross-listings are applied (PAM 2000/2100/2101 = PUBPOL 2000/2100/2101, BTRY 3010 = STSCI 2200, BTRY 3080 = STSCI/ILRST 3080). Smaller issues are outdated or garbled descriptions and an unencoded rule that foundation courses must be done by the sixth semester.

chemical-engineering-bs.summary:
The chemE.ts file is out of date and contains copy-paste errors.
- **Semester 8:** the description says CHEME 4620, but the checker duplicates Semester 5. Because Semester 5 allows double counting, Semester 8 shows as complete without CHEME 4620.
- **Missing course:** CHEME 2200 is not required anywhere.
- **Unfulfillable slot:** Semester 4 requires CHEM 3090, which is no longer in the roster.
- **Computing:** CS 1110 is rejected; only CS 1112 is accepted.
- **Advanced CHEME electives:** the list is badly outdated in both directions.
- **Major-approved electives:** 3 credits are required instead of 9.
- **Biology elective options:** some are stale (BIOG 1107/1108) or incomplete (BIOG 1445, AP score).
- **Chemistry and physics alternatives:** the AP Chem + CHEM 2080/2081 path and PHYS 2217 are missing.

chemistry-ba.summary: The CoursePlan Chemistry file does not match the 2026-2027 catalog in several places that change what counts. Missing pieces: the general chemistry labs (CHEM 2071, CHEM 2081), the PHYS 1110 lab in physics sequence 2, and CHEM 3880 in physical chemistry, so a single CHEM 3870/2870 counts for every student. The file also keeps a retired organic option (CHEM 3530). The catalog's 60-credit (57 for class of 2027) elective structure, which accepts any CHEM course at 4000 level or above and caps research at 4 credits, is replaced by invented track-based course counts with a fixed list. That list includes a core course (CHEM 2880/3880) and lets an 'Honors' option need 0 electives. The 8-credit lab rule is reduced to one course.

civil-engineering-bs.summary:
The ce.ts file is badly out of date against the 2026-2027 catalog. The nine core courses match. However:
- The Capstone Design Elective list is almost entirely different: only CEE 4740 overlaps.
- The Design Elective list shares only BEE 4730 with the catalog.
- The Major-Approved Elective list is missing 16 catalog courses and accepts about a dozen courses the catalog no longer lists.
- The second engineering-distribution slot is wrongly restricted to a short list. With double counting allowed, BEE 2510 can count as both ENGRD and core without the extra major-approved elective the catalog then requires.
- The core-course substitutions (Smart Cities, Civil Infrastructure), the design-context diversity rule and the major's Technical Communication course are not represented.
- Descriptions and source URLs are stale.

climate-change-minor.summary: All 31 courses in the 2026-2027 catalog list are accepted by the file, either directly or through cross-listings (PLSCS 4290 = PLSCI 4290, BEE 4800 = EAS 4800, NTRES 3030 = EAS 3030). The BEE 2000 seminar, one-course-per-category rule (Categories 1-3), 18-credit total, unstructured-credit cap and AP exclusion are all encoded. However, the file has drifted from the catalog. It accepts several courses the catalog does not list: NTRES 6240, PLSCS 5290, GOVT 3061/AMST 3061, SYSEN 5120/5210/5240, CEE 6648 and LAW 4444. It adds a 12-credit 3000-level-or-higher requirement the catalog does not have. Its descriptions also state a one-1000-level-course limit and a C- grade rule that the catalog does not mention.

cognitive-science-minor.summary: The CoursePlan file for the Cognitive Science minor does not match the 2026-2027 catalog. The intro requirement accepts COGST 2200 (HD 2200) where the catalog names COGST 2350, so COGST 2350 cannot count. The file asks for three upper-level courses where the catalog requires four. The upper-level checker only accepts COGST-coded courses, so most of the catalog's non-COGST sample courses are rejected. It also adds a required Lab Requirement that the catalog describes only as encouraged. The two-department rule and the 15-credit minimum are not encoded.

communication-bs.summary: The CoursePlan file follows an older Communication curriculum and is out of date. Main problems: COMM 1111 is missing from Foundations. Only 2 of the 4 core courses are required instead of 3. The upper-level requirement is split into concentration credits (6) plus a fixed elective list (9 credits) instead of 4 COMM courses at 3100+. The file does not exclude COMM 4960/4980, does not cap COMM 4970/4990, and accepts non-COMM and 2000-level codes as electives. It also keeps two requirements the catalog does not have: a broad separate statistics requirement and an FWS requirement.

computer-science-ba.summary: The CS core and the two-course CS elective rule match the 2026-2027 catalog for current students. The file still disagrees with the catalog in several places. The A&S Math requirement (Calc I, Calc II, linear algebra) is missing entirely. The practicum checker rejects five courses the catalog lists (CS 5121, 5321, 5411, 5621, 5740) and accepts unlisted ones (CS 4154, CS 5431, any CS 4**1). The CS Electives checker does not exclude CS 4997 or enforce the 3-credit minimum. The Technical Electives checker rejects the one allowed 2000-level course and does not exclude CS 4090/4997/4998. The Major-approved Elective accepts AP/IB credit and ROTC courses the catalog bars.

computer-science-bs.summary: The CS major file broadly follows the 2026-2027 catalog: the core, two 4000+ CS electives, technical electives, external specialization and the major-approved elective are all present. Several differences remain. The most serious is the practicum/project list, which rejects five courses the catalog now accepts (CS 5121, CS 5321, CS 5411, CS 5621, CS 5740) and still accepts retired or dropped courses. The major-approved elective does not block AP/IB credit, which the catalog forbids. Other gaps: CS 4997 is not excluded from CS electives, the technical electives ignore the one-2000-level allowance and the CS 4090/4997/4998 exclusions, the 3-credit minimum per elective is never checked, the external specialization's limit on CS cross-listed courses is not mentioned, and there is no CS-specific MATH 2940 requirement.

computer-science-minor.summary: Requirements 1 and 2 match the catalog once cross-listings are applied (ECE 2400 = ENGRD 2140; ECE 3140 = CS 3420). The elective requirement has three problems. It rejects CS 2802, which the catalog accepts alongside CS 2800. It rejects CS 3110, CS 3410 and CS 3420 outright, so a student who takes two of them cannot count the second as an elective. It does not enforce the 18-credit minimum for the minor.

data-science-minor.summary: The CoursePlan Data Science minor file is substantially out of date compared with the 2026-2027 catalog. The overall structure matches the catalog: one Core Statistics course, one Core Computing course, and four category courses covering at least three categories. The course lists do not match. Every requirement is missing current catalog courses, including ECON 3130 for Core Statistics, AEM 2820, AEM 2850 and HADM 3710 for Core Computing, and many Data Analysis, Ethics, Data Communication and Domain Expertise courses. Every requirement also accepts courses the catalog no longer lists, several of them still offered (AEM 2010, AEM 2011, HADM 4760, ECE 4520, INFO 4270, COMM 3189, EAS 3540). Some courses sit in the wrong category, courses the catalog lists in two categories are only usable in one, and the 18-credit minimum is not encoded. The category breakdown is inferred from the order of the parsed table, which merged all four category tables under 'Core Computing'.

design-environmental-analysis-bs.summary: The DEA data file follows an older catalog and does not match the 2026-2027 requirements. Core courses are wrong in both directions: it asks for DEA 1050 and DEA 5304, and omits DEA 1141, DEA 1501, DEA 2025 and DEA 4800. DEA 3550 sits in a separate requirement that also accepts ILROB 4710 and PAM 3120. The thematic list is outdated: courses are missing, retired codes are extra, and the one-per-area rule is not enforced. The Human Development/Psychology requirement lacks HD 1130. The Humanities checker uses the wrong distribution list. Natural Science II and Additional Distribution use retired distribution codes, so most qualifying courses are rejected. Physics accepts PHYS 1101/1102. Natural Science I tells students AP counts, which the catalog forbids. The 11-credit Outside of Design and Environmental Analysis requirement is missing entirely.

design-environmental-analysis-minor.summary: The DEA minor file disagrees with the 2026-2027 catalog in its core courses. Slot 1 requires DEA 1050, which the catalog does not list and which was last offered FA23. Slot 2 accepts DEA 1101 and DEA 1200/2200 but rejects the catalog's DEA 1110 (COGST 1111). The DEA 1500 slot does not accept DEA 1501. The file also lacks the required DEA studio course and the 15-credit minimum in DEA courses, and the core description does not match its checker. The upper-level thematic list cannot be checked because the catalog defers the eligible courses to a form.

dyson-business-minor-engineers.summary: The data file has the right six-part structure and credit totals (3+3+3+3+1.5+3 = 16.5), but it is out of date with the 2026-2027 catalog in several places. Introduction to Basic Business Concepts is missing NCC 5540 and accepts courses the catalog no longer lists (ENGRI 1270/MAE 1270 and ORIE 4152/ENGRG 4610/MAE 4610). Career Goals uses a fixed, outdated list of courses. The catalog instead accepts any AEM, HADM, NBA or NCC course at 3000+ taken for a letter grade. As a result the file wrongly accepts BEE 4890 and rejects every HADM, NBA and NCC upper-level course and many AEM ones. The ORIE-only restriction on ORIE 3150 and the ban on ORIE majors using AEM 3100 are not encoded, and the 9-credits-at-Cornell rule is missing.

earth-atmospheric-sciences-minor.summary: The required EAS 2250 course and the core list mostly match the catalog. Three things are wrong. The core checker also accepts EAS 3450, which the catalog does not list. The additional-courses requirement asks for one course instead of two. That requirement also never checks the subject, so any non-EAS course at the 3000 level or above satisfies it. The 18-credit minimum is not enforced either.

earth-climate-sciences-ba.summary: The eas.ts file does not match the 2026-2027 catalog. It still accepts MATH 1110/1120, a CHEM 1570-only path and PHYS 2214 for chemistry. It drops BIOG 1440 because BIOG 1140 is listed twice. The Environmental core uses EAS 3450 instead of EAS 4710, and the Ocean core uses EAS 3010 instead of EAS 3030. All four elective lists differ substantially from the catalog. The field-course rule is reduced to 3 credits of any EAS course. Several descriptions are stale.

earth-climate-sciences-ecsag-bs.summary:
The EAS data file follows an older version of the Earth and Climate Sciences major and disagrees with the 2026-2027 catalog in many places. The data file has these problems:
- **Mathematics:** it accepts MATH 1110/1120.
- **Physics:** it does not allow mixing the alternatives.
- **Chemistry:** it accepts CHEM 1570 alone or PHYS 2214.
- **Biology:** it omits BIOG 1440.
- **Core courses:** the Environmental and Ocean core courses are wrong.
- **Elective lists:** every concentration's elective list both misses current catalog courses and accepts courses the catalog does not list, including a nonexistent BEE 4840 and core courses counted again as electives.

earth-climate-sciences-ecsen-bs.summary: The eas.ts file is out of date against the 2026-2027 catalog for the Engineering Earth and Climate Sciences BS. The biggest problems are in the concentrations: the Environmental Science and Ocean Sciences cores list the wrong courses, and all four elective lists differ substantially from the catalog. The Chemistry options let CHEM 1570 or PHYS 2214 alone satisfy the whole requirement. Biology rejects BIOG 1440 because of a duplicated BIOG 1140. Mathematics accepts MATH 1110/1120 and omits MATH 2930/2940. Physics does not accept mixed pairs, and the Field Work requirement does not reflect the per-concentration field course rules.

economics-ba.summary: Core courses and the 12-course total match the catalog. Several problems remain. The 4000-level and 12-course checkers accept ECON 4997, ECON 4998 and ECON 4999, which the catalog excludes from the twelve courses. The 4000-level checker also counts every graduate ECON course. The 12-course checker accepts every 5000- and 6000-level ECON course, even though the catalog limits graduate courses to a department list. Neither checker accepts the one ECON 2400–2999 course the catalog allows. Finally, an 'Admission to the Major' requirement adds MATH 1110, which the catalog does not mention.

electrical-computer-engineering-bs.summary: The ECE data file does not match the 2026-2027 catalog in several places that change what counts. The third foundation course is fixed to ECE 3140, while the catalog allows any of five. The CDE list accepts ECE 4250 and ECE 4370, which the catalog does not list. The ECE elective structure is 3 courses at 4000-level plus 1 at 3000-level with no credit floor, against the catalog's 5 courses and 17 credits (2 at 4000+ and 3 at 3000+). The file also keeps two requirements the catalog no longer has (Advanced Programming and Probability & Statistics). Finally, the Outside-ECE technical elective checker accepts ECE courses and does not enforce the 3-credit 3000-level portion.

electrical-computer-engineering-minor.summary: The data file differs from the 2026-2027 catalog in two places. It has no requirement for CS 3410, which the catalog table lists as its own item. Its first 'choose two' list offers ECE 2200 instead of ECE 2720. The 3000-level and 4000-level elective checkers broadly match the catalog's 'non-project technical' rules, but their descriptions are worded differently. The catalog does not say which courses count as project courses.

engineering-physics-bs.summary: The core AEP list and the 2-of-3 choice (AEP 3560/3620/4340) match the catalog. Four things do not. The circuits requirement accepts an ECE 2100 + ECE 2300 alternative the catalog does not offer. The PHYS 4410 substitute accepts AEP 3300, which the catalog names only in its overlap caveat. The elective checker rejects the one any-level elective the catalog allows. The independent-study cap and the 9-credits-outside-AEP rule are not enforced. Sources and some labels are also outdated.

english-ba.summary: engl.ts encodes the old English major (40 credits, 12 pre-1800 credits, 8 credits at 4000 level, a 12-credit concentration). The 2026-2027 catalog requires at least ten courses and 30 credits. It also requires distribution courses: two ENGL-PRE, two ENGL-PST, one ENGL-GLS and two ENGL-LOA, with at least one LOA course on American Indian/Indigenous, African American, Asian American, Pacific Islander or Latina/o literature. Further requirements are two 4000-level Cornell ENGL seminars and a three-course concentration. The file has no Post-1800, Global South or Literatures of the Americas requirements. Its credit thresholds would show catalog-compliant students as incomplete. Its checkers mishandle 1000-level courses, honors tutorials and the 3-credit minimum. Its descriptions and sources reflect the old department guide.

environmental-engineering-bs.summary: The envE.ts file is out of date with the 2026-2027 catalog. The biggest problems: it treats BEE 2220 and ENGRD 3200 as alternatives (and adds ENGRD 2210) when the catalog requires both courses. It requires CEE 4510, which the catalog no longer lists. It asks for two major-approved electives instead of three. It rejects catalog-listed BIOSM 1610, BIOSM 1780 and BEE 3710 while accepting EAS 4800 and CHEM 3530, which the catalog does not list. It also leaves out the capstone rule for design electives, has a malformed lab course code, carries an outdated ENGRD recommendation, and has no item for the EHS Lab Safety Training.

fashion-design-management-bs.summary:
The fsad.ts file is substantially out of date compared with the 2026-2027 catalog. It encodes only an older version of Option I (Fashion Design) and leaves out Option II (Fashion Design Management) entirely. Within Option I, several things are wrong:
- The core list is wrong: it adds FSAD 1111, FSAD 4700 and FSAD 4770 and omits FSAD 3320.
- The Advanced Studios requirement and the 11-credit Outside Fashion Design and Management requirement are missing.
- The upper-level FSAD electives use the wrong levels.
- The Psychology, Statistics, Natural Science I and Ethics/Sustainability course lists accept courses the catalog does not and reject courses it does.
- Natural Science II and Additional Distribution use obsolete distribution codes.
- Social Science omits GDEV.
- The Art History check also accepts ART courses because of how `ifCodeMatch` handles shorter subject codes.

food-science-bs.summary: The foodsci.ts file reflects an older Food Science curriculum and differs substantially from the 2026-2027 catalog. Key gaps: FDSC 2000 is required instead of FDSC 2005, and FDSC 4240 and the CHEM labs are missing. Elective credit totals and course lists are wrong. The Business focus is built around marketing, accounting, finance and business-elective slots the catalog no longer has, and lacks the Business-only chemistry path. Both Business and Safety require FDSC 5970, which was last offered FA21. The Science focus does not require MATH 1120. There are also extra or missing alternatives: CHEM 2150, MATH 1710, PHYS 1101, ORIE 2380 and ENTOM 4250 are accepted, while BIOMG 1350, PHYS 1110/1112 and ENTOM 4520 are not.

game-design-minor.summary: The two required-course slots mostly match the catalog. The additional-courses list does not. The checker misses many catalog courses: all the HD courses, most PMA courses, PSYCH 1102/1131/2580/4150/4500, SYSEN 5420 and VISST 2000. It also accepts several courses the catalog no longer lists: INFO 4275, PMA 3531/3533/3614/3631/3880, and a number of PSYCH 3xxx/4xxx courses. Blanket ART 1–3xxx and MUSIC wildcards let in unlisted courses. Requirement 2 still accepts the discontinued CS/INFO 4154, and the 18-credit minimum is not encoded.

government-ba.summary: The Government major file is out of date with the 2026-2027 catalog. The catalog requires one course in 3 of the 4 subfields (AM, CP, PT, IR), and the file has no such requirement. The file encodes 28 credits at the 2000+ level plus a separate 3-credit 'Tenth Government Course', which the catalog no longer describes; the catalog asks for 30 additional GOVT credits with at most one 1000-level course. The seminar requirement accepts any GOVT course numbered 4000 or above instead of the published GOVT-SEM list. The rule allowing GOVT 1615 or GOVT 1616 but not both is not enforced. The intro requirement's five accepted courses (GOVT 1111, 1313, 1615, 1616, 1817) and its count of two match the catalog.

health-policy-minor.summary: The data file still encodes the old PAM-based Health Policy minor. The PUBPOL 2350 core is still accepted through its cross-listing. However, the 9-credit HCP-EL elective list is badly out of date: many current HCP-EL courses are rejected, and several non-listed courses (5000-level PAM courses, PAM 4140, PAM 4230, PAM 4280) are accepted. The 'additional course' checker only accepts PAM-subject courses, so most PUBPOL-only courses are rejected, and it does not cap the level at 4000. Names, descriptions and the source URL also still refer to PAM and the old Human Ecology page.

history-ba.summary: The CoursePlan History major file has the right three headline requirements: four world-area courses, three pre-1800 courses and two seminars. It does not enforce what the 2026-2027 catalog actually requires. The world-area requirement accepts any HIST course instead of one course from each of four of the five HIST-HAN/HNA/HEU/HGS/HTR categories. The seminar requirement accepts any HIST course and does not enforce the 4000-level seminar or the published seminar number ranges. The file has no requirement for the overall nine courses and 30 credits. It also forbids double counting, which the catalog explicitly allows. The description still refers to the classes of 2019–2021.

hotel-management-bs.summary: The CoursePlan file follows an older Hotel Administration curriculum and is out of date. Several core course lists use retired course numbers. The HADM Electives credit count is wrong and its checker accepts only 3000-level courses. The Free Electives count and several descriptions contradict the catalog. The file is also missing the Additional Distribution Electives, Ethics, Diversity & Inclusion and Practice Credit requirements.

human-development-bs.summary: The data file still encodes the 2020-2021 HD curriculum sheet, and most requirements are out of date. Intro now requires HD 1130, not HD 1150/1170. A Developmental Psychology requirement (two of five courses) and the 11-credit Outside of HD requirement are missing. The breadth, depth and elective structure and credit counts differ. The Research Methods, Statistics and Natural Science I course lists are wrong. The distribution-code checkers for Social Science, Humanities, Natural Science II and Additional Distribution omit the A&S and some CALS codes the catalog accepts.

human-development-minor.summary: The HD minor file has the right overall shape: one introductory course plus 4 more HD courses (5 total), with HD 4000/4010/4020/4030 excluded. However, the introductory requirement lists outdated courses. It accepts HD 1100, HD 1150 and HD 1170 instead of the catalog's HD 1130, HD 2150 and HD 2170, so no current student can fulfil it. The 6-credit upper-level rule cannot be confirmed because the catalog does not show the required amount.

inequality-studies-minor.summary: The data file for the Inequality Studies minor is out of date against the 2026-2027 catalog. The core course requirement is correct. The overview course list is missing three catalog options (GOVT 3251, PUBPOL 2250, PUBPOL 2370) and accepts several courses the catalog does not list (ECON 3450/ILRLE 4426, PAM 3370/SOC 3370, ILROB 6260, PAM 4470/SOC 4470). The Health Equity Track is only mentioned in the description and is not modelled. None of the five health-equity sample electives (AEM 1600, ANTHR 2424, BSOC 2051, NS 1150, PUBPOL 3280) is accepted by the elective checker. The rule that courses must span at least three departments is not shown anywhere. The elective list also accepts the required core course and contains a few codes that are not in the roster.

information-science-ba.summary: The INFO data file follows an older version of the major and differs from the 2026-2027 catalog in many places. Core is missing INFO 2951, and Programming is missing CS 1112. The Statistics list accepts many courses the catalog no longer lists. Every concentration's course lists have drifted: dropped courses are still accepted and newly listed ones are missing. Interactive Technologies does not require CS 2110. Digital Culture and Production merges its two options into one rule that accepts combinations the catalog does not allow. Electives omit several approved lower-level courses, still accept INFO 4910 and INFO 4997, and do not enforce the 3-credit minimum.

information-science-bs.summary: The CALS Information Science data file is out of date against the 2026-2027 catalog. Core does not accept INFO 2951. Programming does not accept CS 1112. Statistics accepts many courses the catalog dropped. The Interactive Technologies concentration omits the required CS 2110. Digital Culture and Production uses the wrong combination rule. Every concentration's course lists have drifted: many current catalog courses are missing and many retired or non-listed courses are accepted. The Electives requirement misses INFO 2310, INFO 2770, INFO 2921, MATH 2310 and MATH 2940, wrongly accepts INFO 4910 and INFO 4997, and does not enforce the 3-credit minimum. Several descriptions and source URLs still describe the old or A&S version of the major.

information-science-minor.summary: The data file has the right Engineering structure: one core, three concentration courses and one elective. Its course lists are badly out of date against the 2026-2027 catalog. Every concentration is missing several courses that are currently offered, and most still accept retired courses the catalog no longer lists. The Data Science core omits INFO 2951. The Digital Culture and Production core accepts only INFO 3561, last offered SP21, and omits the six alternatives the catalog now allows. The Information Ethics, Law, and Policy concentration list accepts STS 4040, which the catalog does not list there. The elective checker accepts only INFO-subject courses, so non-INFO concentration courses such as CS 3780 or ECON 4020 are rejected.

information-science-systems-technology-b.summary: The ISST data file is out of date against the 2026-2027 catalog. The core requires INFO 2300 where the catalog requires INFO 1300. The ML core option and several concentration groups omit ORIE 3741. Almost every concentration group is missing current courses and accepts courses the catalog no longer lists. Behavioral Science is encoded as any three courses instead of one each from A, B and C. The CS 2800 requirement is not enforced. The major-approved elective list reflects an old area scheme rather than 'any concentration course'.

linguistics-ba.summary: The foundation courses, the six-course structure (at least 2 at 3000+, at most 1 at the 1000 level) and the two ancillary skills courses match the catalog. Several catalog rules are missing or loosened in the file. The 37-credit minimum for the ten linguistics courses is not checked. A 3-credit CU-UGR course is accepted where the catalog requires four credits. A CU-UGR course below the 3000 level can never count. Language courses with a LING prefix are not excluded. Other-department petition courses have no path to count. Some descriptions are inaccurate.

linguistics-minor.summary: The LING 1101 and foundation-course requirements match the catalog. The three additional-course slots (3000+, 2000+, any level except LING 1101, each 3+ credits) correctly encode the catalog rule of at least one course at 3000+ and no more than one at the 1000 level. The file does not enforce the 18-credit minimum. It also accepts only LING-subject courses (and their cross-listings), not other courses approved for the linguistics major. It has no reminder of the B- grade prerequisite, and one description is misworded.

materials-science-engineering-bs.summary: The MSE file follows an older department curriculum and is out of date with the 2026-2027 catalog. The catalog requires one Category 2 ENGRD; the file requires both MSE 2610 and MSE 2620. The core list adds MSE 3010 and omits MSE 2010, 2020, 2030 and 2110. The file keeps junior courses the catalog no longer lists (MSE 3120, ENGRC 3111, MSE 3070). Senior Design also accepts MSE 5070. The file asks for three application electives where the catalog asks for four, and it keeps an Advanced Math requirement the catalog does not have. The Senior Lab/Thesis toggle, the two-category application rule and the outside technical elective broadly match.

mathematics-ba.summary: The Mathematics BA file is out of date against the 2026-2027 catalog. The Algebra and Analysis lists are close, but MATH 3270 is missing from Analysis, and the requirement that at least two of the nine courses be 4000-level MATH is not encoded. Several concentration options are out of date. Mathematics and Applied Mathematics reject most non-MATH 'mathematical models' courses. Applied Mathematics leaves out the Group A–D distribution rule and the second-models-course alternative. The Computer Science, Economics, Biology, Operations Research and Statistics course lists each miss current catalog courses and accept retired or unlisted ones. The Statistics 'at most one' limits are not enforced. The Physics concentration matches.

mathematics-minor.summary: The Mathematics minor file follows the catalog's overall structure: linear algebra and multivariable calculus prerequisites, then four MATH courses at 3000 or above, with one in algebra, one in analysis and at least one at the 4000 level. Several course lists and rules have drifted from the 2026-2027 catalog. The linear algebra prerequisite does not accept MATH 2310. The analysis list is missing MATH 3270 and adds MATH 3230. The algebra list adds MATH 4315 and MATH 4560. The MATH 4*** wildcard lets in MATH 4900, MATH 4980 and MATH 4997, which the catalog excludes. The prerequisite grade minimums (B-, or B+ for MATH 2310) are not shown to students anywhere.

mechanical-engineering-bs.summary: The ME data file is out of date in most major-specific lists. ENGRD 2210 is missing from the required courses, and the Probability and Statistics requirement is missing entirely. The major-approved elective, senior design and math elective lists all accept courses the 2026-2027 catalog does not list, and all omit currently offered courses the catalog does list. The technical elective does not enforce the 3-credit minimum and does not include the 1000-level biology courses the catalog accepts. Only the Required Major Courses list and the ENGRD 2020 requirement match the catalog.

nutritional-sciences-bs.summary:
The ns.ts file is out of date against the 2026-2027 Nutritional Sciences catalog. Several requirements would give students wrong results:
- Introductory Chemistry ignores the labs and options B/C.
- Advanced Electives counts 3 courses instead of 9 credits and omits several eligible NS courses.
- Statistics accepts MATH 1710.
- Organic Chemistry accepts CHEM 3530.
- The 'Communications' checker accepts every course because of a function-reference bug.
- 'Communications' and 'Social Sciences and Humanities' are old CALS-style requirements the major no longer has.
- The major's FWS requirement and the Human Ecology-only 11-credit Outside Nutritional Sciences requirement are missing.
The Organic Chemistry Lab, Physiology, Biochemistry and NS Core requirements match.

operations-research-engineering-bs.summary: The ORIE data file covers the required ORIE core courses correctly. It is out of date against the 2026-2027 catalog in several ways. The new 'Focused Elective Courses in Data, Decisions, and AI' block is missing. So are the major-specific math requirements (MATH 2940 plus one of MATH 2930/CS 2800/MATH 3040). ENGRD/CS 2110 is treated as only 'recommended' when the catalog requires it. The ORIE Electives checker ignores the catalog's exclusions, its inclusions (ORIE 3320, ORIE 3741, CS 4999) and its credit caps. The Major Approved Electives entry does not reflect the Category A, outside-ORIE or research-cap rules, and its name contradicts its checker.

operations-research-management-science-m.summary: The core requirement matches the catalog: at least three of ENGRD 2700, ORIE 3300, 3310, 3500, 3510 and 4580. The elective requirement has two problems. First, its checker rejects the core ORIE courses, but the catalog lets a fourth core course count as one of the three electives. The description shown to students says the opposite of what the checker does. Second, the file omits the footnote capping ORIE 4900, 4999 and 4990 combined at three credits. It also counts courses only and never checks the 18-credit minimum.

philosophy-minor.summary: The data file splits the five-course PHIL minor into separate slots: 2 courses at 3000+, 1 history course, 1 course at 2000+, and 1 course at 1000+. This correctly limits students to one 1000-level course, requires two at the 3000 level or higher, and excludes FWS and X9XX courses, as the 2026-2027 catalog says. The differences are mostly in what students are told: one description promises an FWS exception that the checker (and the catalog) do not allow, the 3000-level threshold is worded as "above 3000", and the cap of two courses from other institutions is mentioned but not checked or flagged. The history-before-1900 slot accepts only PHIL 2200 and PHIL 2220, with a checkerWarning saying other courses may count.

physics-ba.summary: The Physics major data file has the overall structure right: the intro sequence, the 3316/3317 and 3318/3327 pairs, a 3-credit lab, and an inside/outside concentration toggle. Several of its course lists and counts no longer match the 2026-2027 catalog. The Mathematics checker is missing MATH 3270 and MATH 2310 and accepts MATH 3230 and MATH 1220, which the catalog does not list. The Physics Lab list is missing most catalog options and accepts two that are no longer listed. The required intro labs PHYS 1110 and PHYS 2210, and the conditional PHYS 2216, are not checked. The inside concentration asks for 15 PHYS credits instead of 21 credits, rejects the AEP math courses, and enforces none of its required parts. The outside concentration does not enforce the 8-credit 3000+ rule.

psychology-ba.summary: The data file is out of date with the 2026-2027 catalog. It has no Research Methods/Scientific Literacy requirement and no 3000-level/4000-level depth requirement. Its breadth requirement uses three fixed slots instead of 'one course in three of four areas', and it omits the Development area entirely. The breadth course lists also differ sharply from the catalog tables: many listed courses are missing and many old or unlisted courses are accepted. The 40-credit requirement does not apply the 12-credit cap on PSYCH 4700/4710.

psychology-minor.summary: The data file matches the catalog's 18-credit total in PSYCH courses and excludes AP credit. It does not enforce the catalog's 6-credit cap on PSYCH 4700/4710 research credits. Its breadth recommendation also names three areas instead of the catalog's three-of-four areas.

public-policy-bs.summary: The data file still encodes the 2020-2021 Human Ecology PAM curriculum, not the 2026-2027 Brooks School Public Policy B.S. It is out of date throughout. The core list is wrong and incomplete: PAM 2300 and PAM 3300 are required, and PUBPOL 1111, 2301, 2370 and 2830 are missing, as is the two-of-three global/comparative group. The electives requirement uses the wrong credit total, course levels, subject and exclusions. Engaged Learning is missing. Several retired requirements remain: Additional PAM Electives, HD/PSYCH, a second Natural Science requirement, an Ethics course list, and 6 credits of distribution-area courses. The Government and Mathematics checkers accept the wrong sets of courses.

public-policy-minor.summary: The data file is out of date. The gateway requirement accepts only GOVT 3032 and omits GOVT 3583. The methods requirement still uses an old list: it accepts GOVT 3990, which the catalog does not list, and omits GOVT 3282 and GOVT 2309. The elective checker accepts any course. Neither it nor its description reflects the rule that at least four of the five courses must be in Government, with at most one outside course allowed with advisor approval.

robotics-minor.summary: The Robotics minor file is badly out of date compared with the 2026-2027 catalog. All four Specialization categories and the Fundamentals list are missing many accepted courses, including Fast Robots, Robot Perception, Robot Learning, Feedback Control, the 5xxx/6xxx equivalents and several newer courses. The file also accepts courses the catalog no longer lists: ECE 3400, MAE 4710, MAE 6790, and CS 4700 under Intelligence. Two of its codes (CS 4752, CS 4790) are no longer offered. Neither footnote (the ME Mechatronics restriction and the independent-research petition) is surfaced to students. The overall structure matches the catalog: 3 Fundamentals, plus 3 Specialization courses from one category, with no double counting.

science-technology-studies-ba.summary: CoursePlan's STS major data does not match the 2026-2027 catalog. The catalog asks for 12 courses: STS 2011, 8 additional STS courses (at least one at the 4000 level or above), and 3 natural science or engineering courses. The file splits the 8 STS courses into level tiers the catalog does not have (1 any-level, 3 at 2000, 2 at 3000+, 2 at 4000+). It also asks for only 2 science courses, and its science checker uses outdated distribution codes that reject most physical-science courses. Smaller problems are a credit minimum the catalog does not state and a broken STS 2011 exclusion.

spanish-ba.summary: The core courses match the catalog. The electives requirement does not. The catalog asks for four eligible electives, one of which is a senior seminar, for eight courses in total. CoursePlan instead requires 15 credits, so a student with four 3-credit electives would show 12/15 and appear unfinished. The electives checker also starts at SPAN 2130 and so rejects SPAN 2097, a course above the SPAN 2095 level. Whether PORT courses or non-SPAN courses count as electives depends on department rules not shown here.

spanish-minor.summary: The language course and the elective count match the catalog. However, the Perspectives requirement is out of date. It rejects SPAN 2140 and SPAN 2150, which the catalog now lists. It still accepts SPAN 2240, which the catalog no longer lists. The elective checker also does not reflect the rule that at least one elective must be taught in Spanish.

urban-regional-studies-bs-urs.summary: The file reflects an older version of the URS major. The core list (CRP 1100/1101/2000/2010/3210) has been fully replaced. The Engaged Learning requirement is missing. The Statistics list omits the default CRP 1200 and accepts several intro stats courses the catalog does not list. The distribution checkers use the old A&S categories (CA/HA/KCM/LA/SBA, MQR only) instead of the catalog's ALC/ETM/GLC/HST/SCD/SSC and DLG/DLS/MQL/SDS/SMR/PHS. The Five CRP Classes wildcard ignores the independent-study exclusion, the 3-credit minimum, the CRP 3348/5348 cap, combined-course pairs and the out-of-department list. The Microeconomics list matches, apart from not limiting the higher-level options to students with AP credit.

viticulture-enology-bs.summary: The VIEN data file is out of date against the 2026-2027 catalog, mostly in the Viticulture & Enology Core. The core requires VIEN 4980, which the catalog does not list. Its final slot asks for VIEN 3300 or VIEN 3200 instead of the catalog's VIEN 4460 or PLSCI 2440. The supervised internship requirement is missing. The Chemistry requirement omits the CHEM 1561 lab. The elective checker is a broad subject-prefix match: it lets in unlisted subjects (HADM, GDEV, any FDSC/VIEN), rejects BIOMI 2911, and does not enforce the 5-credit VIEN minimum. The Biology and Statistics requirements match. Plant Science is accepted correctly through cross-listings but is described with retired codes.
